facts.text: Progress Village established 1958 as one of Florida's first planned African American communities, created during the Civil Rights Movement to provide affordable housing.
Johnson Community Center opened 2016, named for a founding figure, and the Progress Village Foundation bolsters education and civic initiatives amid suburban evolution and planned park enhancements.
Originally designed as a self‑sustaining community, Progress Village included homes, schools, and businesses to support its residents, many of whom were Black professionals and families.
By 1965, families like Bettye Napier’s helped Progress Village grow, offering Black residents an escape from Tampa’s segregated core while Jim Crow restrictions barred them from white neighborhoods.
Progress Village is 9 miles southeast of downtown Tampa, bordered by Palm River‑Clair Mel to the north, Riverview to the east, and Gibsonton to the south.
